questions.question: A 10 kg crate on a rough floor is pulled horizontally with 50 N while friction opposes with 10 N. Run the full free-body method to find the acceleration, and explain why the crate's equal-and-opposite pull on the rope does not stop it accelerating.
questions.expected_answer: Free-body diagram: applied force 50 N forward, friction 10 N backward, weight down, normal force up; vertical forces balance. Choose forward positive. Fnet = 50 − 10 = 40 N. a = Fnet ÷ m = 40 ÷ 10 = 4 m·s⁻² forward. The crate's pull on the rope is a third-law partner acting on the ROPE, a different object — only forces acting ON the crate enter its own free-body diagram, so the pair never cancels.

questions.question: Calculate the electrostatic force between charges of 2 μC and 3 μC placed 0,1 m apart (k = 9 × 10⁹), then use the inverse-square reflex to state the force at 0,2 m without recalculating.
questions.expected_answer: Convert prefixes first: 2 × 10⁻⁶ C and 3 × 10⁻⁶ C. F = kQ₁Q₂ ÷ r² = (9 × 10⁹ × 2 × 10⁻⁶ × 3 × 10⁻⁶) ÷ (0,1)² = 5,4 × 10⁻² ÷ 0,01 = 5,4 N, repulsive since both charges are positive, acting along the line joining them. At 0,2 m the distance has doubled, so the force quarters: 5,4 ÷ 4 = 1,35 N.

questions.question: A 12 V battery feeds a 3 Ω resistor in series with a 4 Ω and 12 Ω parallel pair. Solve the whole network with the collapse-solve-expand drill and close the power ledger.
questions.expected_answer: Collapse: parallel pair = (4 × 12) ÷ (4 + 12) = 3 Ω; total = 3 + 3 = 6 Ω. Solve: I = 12 ÷ 6 = 2 A from the battery and through the series resistor. Expand: V across the series resistor = 2 × 3 = 6 V, leaving 6 V across each parallel branch; branch currents 6 ÷ 4 = 1,5 A and 6 ÷ 12 = 0,5 A, summing to 2 A at the junction. Power ledger: battery delivers 12 × 2 = 24 W; dissipation is 2² × 3 = 12 W, 1,5² × 4 = 9 W and 0,5² × 12 = 3 W, totalling 24 W — the ledger closes, certifying every number.
